put on your best robe

give the little children something.

searching for knowledge with diligence,

you further cultivated virtue,
your body waged a heavy war,

and your drink was only clear water,
your clothes were poor, yet neat,
the spirit always concerned in prayer.

7.

you inherited a very great treasure from them,
which you neither wasted uselessly
nor locked up in an iron chest.

8.

for you did not keep it as your own,
but as steward appointed by the Lord,
thereby also this deed of yours is told:

9.

who had three beautiful daughters by his wife;
but now that they had grown old,
he could no longer maintain them.

with dishonorableness.

11.

threw through the window a bag of gold,
by which one daughter was saved.

12.

through this the second daughter was married,
so great power had this hidden gold.

13.

and at night brought the money into the house,
by which he preserved her body in distress

14.

During fasting you tamed your body,
the flesh was pricked with a hair shirt;
your soul, a temple of the Holy Spirit,
was day and night attached to God.

5.
After you were ordained a priest,
you further pursued virtue,
your body engaged in a hard struggle,
so that it would be more under the spirit.

6.
You slept and ate much less than before,
and your drink was clear water alone,
your clothes were poor, yet neat,
the spirit always concerned in prayer.

7.
When your parents both were dead,
you received from their estate a very great treasure,
which you did not waste uselessly
or lock up in an iron chest.

8.
You gave the poor generously what was theirs,
for you did not keep it as your own property,
but as steward placed by the Lord,
whereby this deed of yours is also told:

9.
In Patara was a poor nobleman,
who had three beautiful daughters with his wife;
but now that they had grown old,
he could no longer maintain them.

10.
So he gave them advice,
which was deadly evil for their souls,
that they for a piece of money
would stain their purity with dishonor.

11.
As soon as Saint Nicholas understood this,
he went at night to the same house,
threw a bag of gold through the window,
by which the one daughter was kept.

12.
Again he returned to the household,
and threw the gold once more through the window;
through which the second daughter was married,
so great power had this hidden gold.

13.
He also remembered the third daughter,
and one night brought the money into the house,
thereby preserving her body in need
and her soul from death.

14.
O wise and merciful prelate,
you know our slippery state,
by which our imprudent young youth
is soon removed from their innocence.

15.
Grant us from God a devout mind,
that always purely does His will;
give us the gold of love in our shoe,
that we may escape the punishment of God's rod.
for him, of money or delicacy
laid in the night before Christmas:
there is found some sugar in it,
some money, some fruit, more or less,
according as it has previously
lived according to father's and mother's will:
for if it has shaved the beast too much
and has been too bad,
Saint Claus will put, in his shoe,
instead of money, a piece of coal."]

Representative_Docs:
["Friends, listen all of you,  
What I am going to sing to you,  
About the sawmill workers here in Steê,  
How they know how to manage their mill:  
But the sailing all depends on the wind,  
In which they take great pleasure,  
Sawmill workers here in Steê,  
Keep your little mill on its course.  

2. Early in the morning we start the work:  
As soon as the wind begins to blow,  
We set our sails together,  
Let our little mill spin skillfully,  
Then we set our beam in place,  
We drink a nice cup of tea,  
Sawmill worker, tighten your saw correctly,  
And do your work with care.  

3. If a saw breaks down again,  
Take a wedge in your hands,  
Put it between the saws,  
So that they do not spoil the wood,  
Or they pull the saw somewhat out,  
They sing a little tune to conclude,  
Friends listen and hear it,  
How it must go with the sawmill workers.  

4. And if there is a small knot in the wood,  
You should quickly wedge it,  
So that you can work unhindered,  
And so that the wood breaks quickly,  
That’s how we do it with the hand bow,  
Sawmill workers, do not be lazy,  
Sawmill workers, secure your beam,  
Before cutting a warp or knot.  

5. And if there is a little gap,  
Let your planks shoot out freely,  
And lay your sled back carefully,  
Sawmill worker, do not let it upset you,  
Then they sharpen the saw slightly,  
So that it goes better through the wood,  
Porter takes away your planks,  
So you lay them properly on the stack.  

6. When the wind suddenly picks up,  
You should then ease half sail or high line,  
Just approve whatever is needed,  
Or how the wind may direct itself,  
Or one lays the sails along the rod,  
Sawmill worker, do not be afraid to ease,  
Sawmill worker, hold fast to your rope,  
So the little mill starts working again.  

7. Porter, if you have taken your planks away,  
Do you want to clear the sawdust from the frames,  
Loosen it so you can work continuously,  
It may be done accordingly,  
And put a brush on the edge,  
And then clean the sand thoroughly,  
And cut well the block,  
It is six and a half inches in the miller's pants.  

8. Friends, listen all,  
How the sawmill workers growl,  
When they are in the mill,  
They hear their saws or spikers rumble,  
And then they pull out the peg,  
And they growl as if half mad.  
They cut, they cut the spikers out,  
They say the work is spoiled after all.  

9. If we have a quiet day,  
We have to lay wood or sawdust,  
Because we always have the load,  
The millers know how to turn their boys,  
Now with one, and now with the other,  
Oh! Those millers are so strange,  
You millers sharpen your saws properly,  
So you can rest once in a while by the way.", "Come friends! Stay a little while,  
I will tell you a strange case,  
How love, through wrongdoing,  
Must descend early into the dark grave.  
Yes friends! Listen to this song,  
And engrave it in your dear children's hearts,  
If you offer love no resistance,  
It often becomes the cause of much suffering. (repeat)  

A farmer lived in Brabant,  
Had fields and cattle and servants and maidens,  
And also a son, a precious possession,  
Who was going to express his love,  
To a young and fresh maidservant,  
He swore to love her forever,  
If only he could win her love,  
To conquer her for his young heart. (repeat)  

He was barely eighteen years old,  
He had to fulfill his duties,  
To go to the draft without fault,  
To avoid any grief,  
He drew a number, but very low,  
Returned sadly to his parents,  
And spoke to this tender maiden:  
Oh love your lover forever tenderly. (repeat)  

The hour of his departure was there,  
That he had to march to the garrison,  
Everyone who cared for him,  
Oh how these bonds tore me apart,  
How hard leaving had to wound him,  
His eyes were full of tears,  
He also said: my dear possessions!  
May God be with you all. (repeat)  

Shortly after, she wrote him a letter,  
And revealed her misfortune;  
Oh come soon beloved,  
You will hardly recognize me,  
Sorrow has eaten through my heart,  
A young son was born to me;  
So wrote this tender maiden,  
To hear of my word of faithfulness. (repeat)  

He read the letter repeatedly,  
And resolved to ask for leave,  
And spoke to his officer,  
For a pass of 14 days.  
He showed the letter to his captain,  
What sorrow his heart had to bear,  
Oh no, said he, that cannot be,  
Wait, your turn will also come. (repeat)  

The young man now became desperate,  
And resolved to desert,  
Come what may,  
I want to honor my beloved,  
Posted at the powder magazine,  
He laid down his rifle and weapons,  
He deserted in the dead of night,  
Ha! thought he, I will soon see my loved one again. (repeat)  

He deserted until dawn,  
When two gendarmes met him,  
One said, show me your pass immediately,  
The young man stood embarrassed.  
They tied him with a cord,  
To transport him to his corps,  
They brought him straight to prison,  
To teach him a lesson for his audacity. (repeat)  

The court-martial was convened immediately,  
And he was sentenced to death,  
His parents undertook the journey,  
To obtain clemency for him,  
His girl, crazed with despair,  
Fell down on her knees there,  
She crawled to the general's feet,  
And sobbed: give me back my lover. (repeat)  

He is the father of my child,  
Show him mercy, have pity on me!  
He is his parents' only child,  
Oh! Bring him back into my arms,  
But the cruel man turned her away,  
And said: no matter how you sigh and cry,  
He who leaves his post in disgrace,  
Is never shown mercy. (repeat)  

The day of punishment came quickly,  
He slowly approached his place of execution,  
A preacher who was his guide,  
Pointed him to our Lord's Prayer,  
He knelt down on the ground,  
And cried: O God! Be my Guardian,  
Be my girl's support and Lord,  
Oh! Strengthen my father and my mother. (repeat)  

The buzzing bullet pierced his heart,  
Put an end to his suffering,  
Everyone shared in his sorrow,  
Many tears were seen flowing,  
Come, youth! Listen to this song,  
And take this sad story to heart,  
If you give love no resistance,  
It early becomes the portion of much suffering. (repeat)", "1.

7. And the linden flower will not heal the heart, only from the lips of the bud, the laughter of the dear girl, when it rings to me.', 'I went to the meadow,
